patterns.hint: Contrast against a claim nobody made; state the positive half on its own.
patterns.example_bad: It's not just a tool, it's a movement.

patterns.hint: Additive contrast; fine once, a tell when it repeats.
patterns.example_bad: The app not only saves time but also delights users.

patterns.hint: Reframe 'X isn't the problem. It's Y'; name Y directly.
patterns.example_bad: The model isn't the problem. It's the data.

patterns.hint: Telegraphed reversal of reasons; give the real reason.
patterns.example_bad: Not because it's cheap. Because it works.

patterns.hint: List of what it is not before what it is; say what it is.
patterns.example_bad: Not a plan. Not a promise. A result.

patterns.hint: Staged transformation arc; describe what changed and when.
patterns.example_bad: Work stops being a chore and starts being a joy.

patterns.hint: Clipped negative tail added for punch; fold it into the sentence.
patterns.example_bad: Deploys in one click, no fuss.

patterns.hint: Announces the content instead of giving it; cut to the content.
patterns.example_bad: Let's dive into the details.

patterns.hint: Throat-clearing before the point; open with the point.
patterns.example_bad: Here's the thing: pricing is broken.

patterns.hint: Standalone candor opener; inside casual talk it's fine, as a set-up it is a tell.
patterns.example_bad: Is it worth it? Honestly? Depends.

patterns.hint: Tells the reader to be impressed; give the fact that would impress them.
patterns.example_bad: We cut costs by half. Let that sink in.

patterns.hint: Flags importance instead of stating the thing; delete the lead-in.
patterns.example_bad: It's worth noting that the deadline moved.

patterns.hint: Stock scene-setting that fits any topic; start with the reader's concrete situation.
patterns.example_bad: In today's fast-paced world, teams need better tools.

patterns.hint: Phrase that delays the point; cut it or say the specific thing.
patterns.example_bad: When it comes to pricing, at the end of the day, value wins.

patterns.hint: Recap ending; finish on the last concrete point or next step.
patterns.example_bad: In conclusion, the project was a success.

patterns.hint: Conclusion section that reruns the text; replace with the next step or cut.
patterns.example_bad: ## Final Thoughts

patterns.hint: Stock 'challenges and outlook' move; name the actual problem and plan.
patterns.example_bad: Despite these challenges, the town continues to thrive.

patterns.hint: Upbeat send-off with no content; end on the last real fact.
patterns.example_bad: The future looks bright for the team.

patterns.hint: Asserts importance; say what depends on it.
patterns.example_bad: Logistics plays a pivotal role in retail.

patterns.hint: Inflates a fact into a symbol or milestone; keep the fact.
patterns.example_bad: The bridge stands as a testament to human ambition.

patterns.hint: Claims a meaning is shown; show the act instead.
patterns.example_bad: The move underscores our commitment to users.

patterns.hint: Trailing -ing phrase adds fake depth; cut it or state a real consequence.
patterns.example_bad: Sales rose 4%, reflecting strong market confidence.

patterns.hint: Word models overuse; swap for a plain word, especially when several cluster.
patterns.example_bad: We delve into a vibrant tapestry of ideas.

patterns.hint: Corporate jargon; use the plain verb or noun.
patterns.example_bad: We leverage synergies to streamline workflows.

patterns.hint: Abstract 'landscape' metaphor; name the market, field or situation.
patterns.example_bad: Navigating the evolving landscape of AI.

patterns.hint: Long verb in place of 'is' or 'has'; use the short one.
patterns.example_bad: The hall serves as a venue and boasts 300 seats.

patterns.hint: Brochure wording; state what the place or product is and has.
patterns.example_bad: Nestled in the heart of the city, the hotel offers stunning views.

patterns.hint: Stock ad phrase; replace with the specific change and a number.
patterns.example_bad: Say goodbye to busywork and unlock the power of automation.

patterns.hint: Unnamed authority; name the source and its finding, or drop the claim.
patterns.example_bad: Experts agree that remote work boosts output.

patterns.hint: Flattery aimed at a chat user; remove.
patterns.example_bad: Great question! The answer is simple.

patterns.hint: Chat wrapper left in standalone text; delete it, keep the content.
patterns.example_bad: Certainly! Here is the revised version.

patterns.hint: An assistant-style service offer may add the author's availability or work. Check the person's own stated or confirmed decision before keeping it: an incoming request or your unconfirmed read-back is not approval. An authorized offer can stay.
patterns.example_bad: Don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions.

patterns.hint: Model talks about itself or its cutoff; remove.
patterns.example_bad: As an AI language model, I cannot browse the web.

patterns.hint: Admits missing data, then guesses; say what is unknown or cut.
patterns.example_bad: While details are limited, she likely grew up in Ohio.

patterns.hint: Dresses an ordinary point as a hidden truth; state the point.
patterns.example_bad: At its core, this is about trust.

patterns.hint: Poster aphorism 'X is the currency of Y'; write the concrete claim.
patterns.example_bad: Attention is the new currency of business.

patterns.hint: Casts the writer as the lone insider; make the claim stand on evidence.
patterns.example_bad: Here's what most people get wrong about hiring.

patterns.hint: Rebuts an objection nobody raised; drop it unless a reader would really object.
patterns.example_bad: Don't get me wrong, docs matter.

patterns.hint: Text narrates its own structure; talk about the subject.
patterns.example_bad: In this article, we'll explore five tips.

patterns.hint: Rhetorical set-up; make the point.
patterns.example_bad: What if I told you onboarding takes five minutes?

patterns.hint: Noun phrase, colon, dramatic reveal; write a plain sentence.
patterns.example_bad: The best part: it learns from you.

patterns.hint: Says something is weighty without naming it; name it.
patterns.example_bad: The implications are significant.

patterns.hint: Two hedges on one claim; keep the one the evidence supports.
patterns.example_bad: This could potentially affect results.

patterns.hint: Says two things are related without saying how; name the relation if the source gives it.
patterns.example_bad: He was associated with the company's growth.

patterns.hint: Inanimate thing acting on its own; name who decided or did it.
patterns.example_bad: The decision emerged after the review.

patterns.hint: Formal connector opening a sentence; most of the time 'also' or nothing works.
patterns.example_bad: Moreover, the plan is cheap.

patterns.hint: Heading in Title Case; use sentence case.
patterns.example_bad: ## Strategic Planning And Global Growth

patterns.hint: Compound adjective after the noun keeps its hyphen; drop it there.
patterns.example_bad: The plan is long-term.

patterns.hint: Round social-proof number with no source; use a measured, sourced figure or cut.
patterns.example_bad: Trusted by 10k+ teams with 99.99% uptime.

patterns.hint: Word-by-word periods for emphasis; write the sentence normally.
patterns.example_bad: Every. Single. Day.

patterns.hint: Empty frame; write the clause itself.
patterns.example_bad: We are worried by the fact that delivery is late.

patterns.hint: 'To' does the same job.
patterns.example_bad: We met in order to agree the budget.

patterns.hint: Empty verb carrying an action noun; use the verb inside the noun: decide, investigate, pay.
patterns.example_bad: The team will conduct an investigation and make a decision.

patterns.hint: Empty subject; start with the real actor or thing.
patterns.example_bad: There are three reasons we missed the date.

patterns.hint: Passive with the actor in a by-phrase; make the actor the subject unless the object is the topic.
patterns.example_bad: The report was prepared by our team.

patterns.hint: Official phrase with a plain equivalent: before, if, now, about, under, attached, by <date>.
patterns.example_bad: Please be advised that prior to the meeting you should sign the form.

patterns.hint: Two words carrying one meaning; keep one.
patterns.example_bad: Here is a short note on the past history of the project.

patterns.hint: Formula apology; name what went wrong, own it and say what happens next.
patterns.example_bad: We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

patterns.hint: Pressure for a reply; give a reason and a date, or make answering easy.
patterns.example_bad: Looking forward to your prompt reply.

patterns.hint: Nudge without content; restate the task, the date and why it matters.
patterns.example_bad: Just following up on my last email.

patterns.hint: Stock opener; start with the point of the letter.
patterns.example_bad: I hope this email finds you well.

patterns.hint: Claim of obviousness: if it is known, cut it; if not, give the evidence.
patterns.example_bad: It's no secret that remote work cuts output.

patterns.hint: Speech repair left in writing; keep only the corrected word.
patterns.example_bad: We sent the report, or rather, its first part.

patterns.hint: Hedge on a figure; give the figure, or the exact figure with an 'as of' date.
patterns.example_bad: We have served more than 200 clients.

patterns.hint: Verbal numbering; in writing a new paragraph or a numbered list does this job (fine in a talk).
patterns.example_bad: Firstly, it is cheap.

patterns.hint: Aside marker: a relevant point needs no flag, an irrelevant one should go.
patterns.example_bad: By the way, humidifiers are on sale.

patterns.hint: Writer decides for the reader; give the fact and let the reader judge.
patterns.example_bad: I'm sure you'll love our new range.

patterns.hint: Corporate or ad cliché; replace it with what actually happens: the step, the number, the client.
patterns.example_bad: We are a team of professionals offering tailored solutions.

patterns.hint: Trait label that tells the candidate nothing; describe the situation that needs the trait.
patterns.example_bad: We want a detail-oriented team player.

patterns.hint: Bait instead of content; say what the reader gets.
patterns.example_bad: You won't believe these jaw-dropping prices

patterns.hint: Talks down to the reader; explain plainly and let them judge the difficulty.
patterns.example_bad: Even a child can set this up.

patterns.hint: Worn idiom used as an image; describe the actual scene.
patterns.example_bad: Late couriers are only the tip of the iceberg.

patterns.hint: Headline that accuses the reader; promise the fix instead.
patterns.example_bad: 5 mistakes you make when ordering furniture

patterns.hint: Stock moral at the end; finish on the last useful point or the next step.
patterns.example_bad: Just start, and remember: you've got this!

patterns.hint: Urgency without a date; give the date and the reason.
patterns.example_bad: Please send the invoice as soon as possible.

patterns.hint: Pressure formula; give the concrete offer, its price and its real deadline.
patterns.example_bad: Act now, while supplies last!

patterns.hint: Intensifier; delete it and see if the sentence lost anything. Keep it if it did.
patterns.example_bad: This is a really very important step.

patterns.hint: The assistant's offer to do more stayed in the text; delete it.
patterns.example_bad: Want me to add a section on pricing?

patterns.hint: Reasoning scaffold leaked into the text; keep only the conclusion.
patterns.example_bad: Let me think about this step by step.

patterns.hint: The sentence restates the previous one; keep the clearer of the two.
patterns.example_bad: In other words, the team shipped late.

patterns.hint: 'Whether you're X or Y' recap that addresses everyone; end on the point for this reader.
patterns.example_bad: Whether you're a founder or a freelancer, this tool fits.

patterns.hint: Question heading in an article; a statement heading tells the reader what the section holds. Fine in a FAQ.
patterns.example_bad: ## Why is caching important?

patterns.hint: Announces a vague list instead of giving the answer; give the answer first.
patterns.example_bad: Generally speaking, smaller PRs merge faster.

patterns.hint: Teaser before the point; state the point.
patterns.example_bad: The catch? It only works on Linux.

patterns.hint: Staged reveal before an ordinary claim; make the claim.
patterns.example_bad: The truth is, nobody reads the docs.

patterns.hint: Tells the reader how to weigh the point instead of showing it; cut it or give the fact that shows it.
patterns.example_bad: That distinction matters.

patterns.hint: Slogan formula standing in for a claim; write the concrete claim.
patterns.example_bad: Design is where art meets engineering.

patterns.hint: Lecturer's distance from the scene; name who does what, or address the reader.
patterns.example_bad: People tend to skip the manual.

patterns.hint: The text narrates its own history or layout; describe the subject as it is. Fine in changelogs and migration guides.
patterns.example_bad: This function was added to replace the old loop.

patterns.hint: Stock outlook; end on the last concrete fact or the stated plan.
patterns.example_bad: The company is poised for growth.

patterns.hint: Filler about missing information or online presence; state what the source shows, or cut the sentence.
patterns.example_bad: He has an active social media presence.

patterns.hint: Leftover hedge beside a confident claim; keep it only where the source shows real doubt.
patterns.example_bad: To some extent, the plan worked.

patterns.hint: Sentence adverb that grades the point; delete it and see whether anything is lost.
patterns.example_bad: Interestingly, the tests passed.

patterns.hint: Contrast split over two sentences; state the second half directly.
patterns.example_bad: It feels like magic. It's actually caching.

patterns.hint: The text labels itself honest or different instead of showing it; delete the label.
patterns.example_bad: Here's an honest breakdown, no fluff.

patterns.hint: Self-help reassurance in a text that is not about feelings; write the advice or the fact plainly.
patterns.example_bad: Missed the deadline? You're not alone.

patterns.hint: The narrator spells out the lesson; end on the event or detail before it.
patterns.example_bad: The moral of the story is simple.

patterns.hint: A run of three or more 'no X' tails; keep the one that states a real condition and do not replace the rest with new tails.
patterns.example_bad: A full report, no guesswork, no surprises, no fees.
